newsitem.title: UK: GEC, BAe tipped for 16 billion pound merger.
newsitem.headline: GEC, BAe tipped for 16 billion pound merger.

text.p: The General Electric Company and British Aerospace Plc are expected to enter talks this year about forming an an alliance that could create a British defence equipment company valued at 16 billion pounds ($26 billion), the Sunday Times newspaper reported.
Government, banking and industry insiders believe the chances are growing of a merger that could produce the fourth largest defence supplier in the western world, it said.
"It's just another piece of speculation," BAe spokesman Mike Peters said. No one at GEC was immediately available to comment.
BAe, expected by analysts to announce a 75 percent increase in its full year profits after exceptional items on Wednesday, has been a favourite target of merger speculation in financial circles.

The speculation intensified after Boeing Co announced plans to merge with McDonnell Douglas Corp in December. Many analysts believe BAe needs to merger with another aerospace or defence group by the end of 1997 in order to compete against the new U.S. aerospace giant.
Last week the French government barred GEC from bidding for Thomson-CSF, the state defence electronics group.

Instead the government wants to forge a national defence and electronics firm by combining CSF with Lagardere Groupe's Matra subsidiary and the military business of Dassault Aerospatiale, the aircraft, missiles and space technology group now being formed.

"If the French government can push through its vision, its new defence combine will dwarf a divided British industry, threatening to reduce the UK firms' influence in the negotiations on cross-border partnerships seen as inevitable in the medium term," the Sunday Time story said.

GEC is worth almost twice BAe in terms of market capitalisation -- 10.4 billion pounds against 5.4 billion -- so GEC investors would get a majority of the new company. They would also receive the bulk of a large special dividend that could accompany a deal, part funded from GEC's some 1.0 billion pound cash resources, said the paper.

Together the groups would have combined defence sales of more than 6.5 billion pounds, behind only American groups Lockheed Martin, Boeing, providing its takeover of McDonnell Douglas goes ahead and Raytheon.

The BAe and GEC's Marconi defence business are complementary, with BAe's expertise as a prime contractor matched by Marconi's pre-eminence in the electronic systems which will account for a growing portion of the value of a ship, aircraft or missile, the article said.
BAe shares closed 32p up at 243p in London on Friday. GEC shares were 7p lower at 376p.
